queries.query: large language model AND network configuration generation OR "network config" "LLM" "configuration synthesis"
queries.rationale: Find primary work where LLMs are used to generate device/router/switch configurations or translate intent to configs; central to NetOps topic.

queries.query: "intent to configuration" OR "intent-to-configuration" OR "natural language" AND "network configuration"
queries.rationale: Locate papers on translating operator intent (natural language) into executable network configuration — operationally meaningful pipeline.

queries.query: LLM AND configuration repair OR "configuration repair" OR "auto-repair" network
queries.rationale: Identify literature on automated detection and repair of misconfigurations using LLMs or program-synthesis approaches (generate–validate–repair patterns).

queries.query: verification OR validator AND network configuration OR "reachability analysis" "header space" "formal verification"
queries.rationale: Gather established formal/deterministic verification techniques used as validators for generated configs (reachability, ACL checks, model checking).

queries.query: verifier-assisted LLM OR "verifier assisted" "LLM" self-correction OR "tool-assisted" "self-correction"
queries.rationale: Search for architectures combining generative models with symbolic/verifier tools for iterative correction (generate→validate→repair loops).

queries.query: agentic OR "autonomous agent" AND "network operations" OR NetOps OR "agentic AI"
queries.rationale: Locate work on autonomous/agentic systems applied to network operations, including orchestration, tool-use, and safety controls.

queries.query: AIOps benchmark OR "NetOps benchmark" OR "network operation benchmark"
queries.rationale: Find existing benchmarks, task suites, and evaluation protocols for AIOps/NetOps to assess external validity and benchmark-adjacent work.

queries.query: LLM benchmark networking OR "LLM for networking" evaluation
queries.rationale: Identify prior attempts to evaluate foundation models specifically on networking tasks to avoid redundant leaderboard-style contributions.

queries.query: failure modes "hallucination" OR "misconfiguration" OR "unsafe action" AND LLM OR "language model" "network"
queries.rationale: Collect literature characterizing failure modes of LLM-driven operational tools: hallucination, incorrect config semantics, unsafe/unsafe-autonomous actions.

queries.query: constrained generation OR "controlled generation" OR "safety filters" AND network configuration OR NetOps
queries.rationale: Search mitigation strategies: constraint-based decoding, schema-guided generation, typed outputs, templates, and guardrails for config generation.

queries.query: simulation environment OR emulation AND network configuration testing OR "Mininet" OR "ns-3" "network emulator"
queries.rationale: Find common emulation/simulation platforms and testbeds used to validate generated configurations and measure operational effects.

queries.query: metrics AND network configuration correctness OR "policy compliance" OR "reachability" OR "connectivity" "validation metric"
queries.rationale: Locate concrete, operational metrics used to measure correctness/safety of configs (reachability, ACL equivalence, performance impact).

queries.query: reproducibility AND LLM experiments OR "prompt documentation" "prompt engineering" "preregistration"
queries.rationale: Collect best practices and methods for reproducible LLM-driven experiments: prompt/version tracking, seeds, preregistration, artifact release.

queries.query: program synthesis OR code LLMs AND network automation OR "network scripts" "configuration synthesis"
queries.rationale: Survey work that leverages code-focused LLMs (Codex, CodeGen) for automation or script generation in network management for analogies and methods.

queries.query: safety "agentic" systems OR "bounded autonomy" AND verification OR "containment" "guard rails"
queries.rationale: Find safety engineering and verification approaches for agentic systems that constrain actions and provide fail-safe behavior relevant to NetOps.

inclusion_criteria: Primary peer-reviewed papers, conference/workshop papers, or preprints (arXiv/SSRN) with accessible full text.
Papers addressing LLMs, generative models, or agentic systems applied to network configuration, NetOps workflows, verification, or AIOps.
Works presenting validators, formal verification, simulation/emulation evaluations, or measurable operational metrics (reachability, policy compliance, connectivity).
Benchmarks, datasets, and task suites for NetOps or AIOps that are publicly available and documented (code/data repositories preferred).
Methodological papers on generate–validate–repair, tool-assisted self-correction, constrained generation, and safety/guardrail mechanisms for generative agents.
Reproducibility and experiment-design guidance for LLM studies (prompt-versioning, seeds, preregistration, artifact release).
Papers from ~2000–2026 with priority to 2017–2026 for LLM-era relevance; allow earlier foundational verification/networking works where directly relevant.
exclusion_criteria: Non-public, proprietary, or NDA-bound reports and internal operator runbooks (not publicly accessible).
Non-scholarly opinion pieces, commercial marketing materials, generic blog posts that lack technical detail or reproducible artifacts (unless they point to primary artifacts).
Works solely about unrelated AI domains (e.g., pure vision models) without transferable methods or clear networking relevance.
Content produced during pre-lock private development runs specific to this programme (permitted per programme only as background but excluded from fresh-evidence corpus).
Papers lacking verifiable bibliographic metadata (title, authors, venue/year) or inaccessible full text for verification.
date_rationale: Prioritize literature from 2017–2026 because transformer architectures (2017) and LLM-driven operational work accelerated after 2019–2020; include earlier foundational networking verification and configuration-analysis works (e.g., header space, formal verification) where they provide essential validators or metrics. This balance captures modern LLM methods and their immediate predecessors while retaining classic verification foundations.
